proposed.explanation: architectural theory does not claim certification is useless; rather it is 'necessary but insufficient.' Certification provides valuable standardization while obscuring complexity. Tension between complexity and measurable standardization, not between regulation and voluntarism. What does this tell you about actual environmental performance?' Certification may not correlate with actual performance. Certification systems...can incentivize easy credits over systemic performance optimization; can subsidize greenification of environmentally problematic building types.' Certifications are 'design-stage projections'—many underperform operationally. The deeper issue: environmental reality is complex (embodied + operational carbon, grid intensity, lifecycle duration); certification systems reduce this to point-systems and marketing categories.
